To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the persuasive eWOM factors are not equally influential among Chinese and Malaysian social media users.
The study found that Chinese and Malaysian students’ attitudes and behavioral intentions to continue their overseas studies were affected by the eWOM messages they received.
Chinese and Malaysians users are more influenced by source attractiveness and source style when processing eWOM messages on social media.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of persuasive eWom messages on users’ attitudes and behavioral intentions.
the impact of persuasive eWOD messages in social media.
the cultural orientations in the context of eWOM messages in SNS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Chinese and Malaysian users differ in the way they perceive and process persuasive eWOM message.

Chinese and Malaysian users have different perceptions and preferences in processing eWOM messages in their decision-making processes, especially when they are exposed to eWOM messages from different sources.
Chinese users were influenced by argument quality, source attractiveness, and source style, while Malaysians were influenced by source credibility and source style.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Chinese and Malaysian users have different attitudes and behavioral intentions toward the eWOM messages, which is due to the different cultural values of the two groups.

argument quality, perceived source credibility, source attraction, source perception, source style, attitude, and intention to continue overseas studies are all important factors that influence Chinese users’ and Malaysian users’ decision to study abroad.
Chinese and Malaysian users are influenced by different persuasive factors when processing eWOM messages in social media.
The main takeaway from our work is that
eWOM messages are more effective when they are persuasive and credible.
the cultural orientation of users should not be ignored when designing and developing persuasive eWOM campaigns in social media.
eWOM source style has a stronger impact on the Chinese users’ attitude and intention to continue studying abroad than on Malaysian users.
